extracted.intended_audience: experimental physicists/chemists and researchers studying galvanism/electrochemistry (19th-century context)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, conducting, and interpreting experiments that test competing theories of galvanism (electric vs chemical), including apparatus controls, choice of reagents, and inference from galvanometric readings. Emphasis on isolating chemical action, verifying polarity, and testing alternative mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of experimental proof
rubrics_metrics.description: "The experimental proofs for the truth of either theory are not sufficiently powerful, to command the assent of all capable of appreciating the weight of such evidence.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require experiments to be sufficiently decisive and reproducible to persuade knowledgeable skeptics; avoid relying on single, ambiguous demonstrations. Provide multiple lines of evidence and controls before drawing strong theoretical conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude alternative (chemical) explanations by control of air/chemical contact
rubrics_metrics.description: "If the compound plate be coated with electric cement to exclude the chemical action of the air on the zinc, I will venture to predict that no decided electric effect will take place.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing whether contact of dissimilar metals alone produces electric effects, explicitly prevent atmospheric/chemical interaction (e.g., coat surfaces with insulating/electric cement) so chemical oxidation cannot be the cause. A valid test must alter only the hypothesized cause while holding other factors constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical validity of inference from experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Taking for granted the truth of the experiment, the conclusion which Volta deduced from it by no means follows as a legitimate inference.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept causal or theoretical conclusions that do not logically follow from the experimental setup. Assess whether alternative mechanisms could account for the observed effect before inferring new laws of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report conducting power of interposed fluids and compare with effect
rubrics_metrics.description: (from Experiment I) "I found that the diluted acid was the most powerful conductor... the electricity generated is greatest when the conducting power of the fluid is least.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify the conductivity of the medium used between electrodes and compare it to galvanic/electric effects; unexpected (non-monotonic) relations between conductivity and observed effect are meaningful counter-evidence to theories that predict direct proportionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use galvanometric direction and standard comparisons to infer polarity
rubrics_metrics.description: References such as "the needle... turned round in the same direction as it does when zinc was substituted..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret galvanometer needle deflections by comparison with standard reference batteries/cells to determine which electrode corresponds to 'zinc' or 'copper' behavior; report direction and magnitude relative to a known standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unintended metallic contact (insulate connections)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent direct metallic contact between conductors when testing for effects due to dissimilar metals in contact; use insulating thread/cement and verify that any electrical/chemical contact is only via the intended conductive path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for gas escape and oxygen involvement (airtight apparatus)
rubrics_metrics.description: (from Experiment VII) "As there is no room for the disengagement of hydrogen... the oxygen of the water cannot combine with the zinc... nevertheless chemical action goes on..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments (e.g., sealed/air‑tight cells) to prevent escape of gases so that putative mechanisms involving atmospheric oxygen or released hydrogen can be tested or ruled out. Report whether gas evolution is possible in the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test chemical specificity by varying acids/solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: "When ... water containing condensed chlorine: a very decided electro-magnetic effect was produced... nitro-muriatic acid... similar effect... nitrous acid... the needle will turn round in the opposite direction.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use different electrolytes/chemicals (diluted sulphuric, nitrous, nitro-muriatic, chlorine-containing water, etc.) to probe how chemical composition of the medium affects polarity and strength of the galvanic effect; unexpected reversals or variations are diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for electrode surface condition and mechanical state
rubrics_metrics.description: (Experiments IV & V) "the furrowed plate corresponds with copper... although greater chemical action..." and "the hard metal in each case corresponds with zinc..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and control for physical/metallic surface condition (smooth, furrowed, hard vs soft, beaten, tempered). Surface roughness, hardness, or work-hardening can change galvanic behavior; report electrode preparation and compare results across surface conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate temperature effects on electrode behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: (Experiment VI) "heated the end... the cold iron was found to correspond with zinc... Since oxygen combines more rapidly with hot than with cold iron, positive electricity ought... to have appeared at the hot iron, whereas the contrary was actually the case.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary electrode temperatures to test theoretical predictions that rely on temperature-dependent chemical reactivity; record temperature and its effect on galvanometer readings to test hypothesized mechanisms (e.g., oxidation rate vs observed polarity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design symmetric/controlled pair experiments (equal discs, mirrored conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: (multiple experiments) use of "two equal discs" or "equal pieces" connected to galvanometer and varying only one factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pairs of equal electrodes or mirror-image setups and change only the single variable under test (metal type, fluid, surface treatment, temperature) to isolate cause-and-effect. Ensure equality of size/shape to avoid spurious asymmetries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be open to revising theory; collect new materials rather than forcing immediate synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: "my object in this paper is rather to demolish old fabrics and collect new materials, from which a more substantial edifice may be raised.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When experimental evidence contradicts prevailing theories, emphasize careful collection and reporting of anomalous data and controlled observations rather than premature construction of a comprehensive new theory; allow future synthesis informed by robust datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for introducing non-algebraic quantities as algebraic definitions when convenient
rubrics_metrics.description: (from Warren's mathematical discussion) "considering sines, cosines, &c., merely as algebraic quantities, we may make use of the expressions sin (a + b), cos (a + b), &c., if such expressions be found convenient in algebraic operations.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In theoretical/mathematical parts of an investigation, it is acceptable to define traditionally transcendental functions (sine, cosine) algebraically for convenience in algebraic manipulations; state such definitions explicitly when used.
